**Ghostdrop v0.2.1** fixes CPU portability of the prebuilt Linux release tarballs.

### Fix

- Pass `-Dcpu=baseline` (overridable via `ZIG_CPU`) when building `libghostty` on Linux in `scripts/build-linux.sh`. Without it, Zig targeted the CI runner's native CPU (emitting ARM SVE instructions on `ubuntu-24.04-arm` that caused `SIGILL` on Apple Silicon VMs and other non-SVE `aarch64` machines, and runner-specific instructions on `x86_64`).

See [v0.2.0](https://github.com/HackToHell/ghostdrop/releases/tag/v0.2.0) for the full release notes (Linux Wayland/X11 support, zero-copy GPU presentation, cross-platform `make install` / `make update`, macOS deadlock fix, FFI isolation, and state-machine hardening).

### Install

#### macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 13+)

1. Download **`Ghostdrop-0.2.1.dmg`** below, open it, and drag **Ghostdrop** onto **Applications**.
2. Builds are ad-hoc signed (not notarized): on first launch use **System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Open Anyway**.

#### Linux (`x86_64` / `aarch64`, glibc >= 2.35)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/HackToHell/ghostdrop && cd ghostdrop
make install RELEASE=v0.2.1    # downloads + verifies tarball into ~/.local
make update                    # git pull + reinstall
```

Or download **`ghostdrop-0.2.1-linux-<arch>.tar.gz`** below and extract into `~/.local`, or on Arch Linux run `make pkg`.

### Verify downloads

```sh
# macOS
shasum -a 256 -c Ghostdrop-0.2.1.dmg.sha256

# Linux
sha256sum -c ghostdrop-0.2.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz.sha256
sha256sum -c ghostdrop-0.2.1-linux-aarch64.tar.gz.sha256
```
